body:
I can't reproduce this problem on an M2 Macbook which indicates it is a GPU/driver-specific. 

I strongly suspect this is an issue of NVidia doing very aggressive shader optimizations that end up causing a slight difference between the shader used for the depth prepass and the shader used for the render pass. 

This issue commonly arises in Vertex shaders with gl_Position. In that case you can use the [`invariant`](https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Type_Qualifier_(GLSL)#Invariance_qualifiers) qualifier. Newer versions of GLSL also have [`precise`](https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Type_Qualifier_(GLSL)#Precise_qualifiers) for situations like your shader. 

I suspect that this could be solved by exposing `precise` to user shaders. 

That being said, I don't think your shader gains anything by using the depth prepass. The depth prepass is nice because it allows you to avoid running the fragment shader for occluded fragments. But, writing to `DEPTH` fully disables that optimization, so you get no benefit from using the prepass. In fact, since the raymarch is expensive, you are essentially doubling the cost of your shader for no practical gain.

> That being said, I don't think your shader gains anything by using the depth prepass. The depth prepass is nice because it allows you to avoid running the fragment shader for occluded fragments. But, writing to DEPTH fully disables that optimization, so you get no benefit from using the prepass. In fact, since the raymarch is expensive, you are essentially doubling the cost of your shader for no practical gain.

Is there a way to reliably disable the depth prepass on a single material without making it go through the transparent pipeline? I couldn't figure out a way to do this, other than using `if (false) discard;` which is likely slower than it needs to be.

I have the same issue using raymarching to fake some 2D sprites to look more 3D. My shader is a box proxy that raymarches a sprite sheet in `fragment()` and writes `DEPTH` from the marched hit position. Symptom is similar as the op - 1px black pepper-like "noise" that looks like TV static when the camera moves even slightly. Disabling Depth Prepass in Rendering->Driver fixes the issue. Specs: `Godot v4.7.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1088) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 61.65 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)` It can be hard to reproduce, it took me days before I noticed it happening. In the editor it often starts after an alt-tab. In the actual game it seems to appear after Ive had the game running for 30mins+, especially if its minimized or in the background while doing something else. Having the editor/game unfocused for a longer period in general seems to contribute to forcing it to happen. Restarting the editor would clear it for a bit and it would happen again in 5 minutes or 1 hour. After enabling it again it came in full force and not even restarting the editor would reset it until disabled Depth Prepass again, making me think there's a caching element invovled. To me it looks something like this: Changing WorldEnviroment Mode from Sky to a Custom color: Red made it change color too. The pattern changes with the circles most subtle movement and is clearly discernable when camera is looking towards the Z-axis and the object is perpendicular to the Z-axis. Viewed from other positions/angles the "rings" are so wide that it's hard to discern the pattern.
